DECISION JOURNAL — this repo keeps one, and you are expected to write to it.

When you make a decision — a point where the work could have gone more than one
way and you picked — record it BEFORE moving on:

  coherence decide "<what you chose>" --over "<what you rejected>" --because "<why>" --session "{{session}}" --agent "{{agent}}"

YOUR SESSION ID IS {{session}}. Pass it on every call — it is what keeps your
decisions attributable to you when four other agents are writing at the same time.

SWARM GYROSCOPE — read the durable field before acting:
  coherence orient
  coherence work inspect

`orient` selects one heading from strict evidence; it does not grant authority.
Only an orchestrator or explicitly authorized coordinator creates or hands off work.
Freeze objective, observable success, risk, authority, owner, dependencies, and scope
before dispatch; add parent/dependency/read/write flags when the boundary grants them:
  coherence work create "OBJECTIVE" --success "OBSERVABLE_RESULT" --risk high \
    --authority orchestrator-delegated --granted-by "ORCHESTRATOR" \
    --boundary "GRANTED_SCOPE" --session "{{session}}" --agent "{{agent}}"
Owners advance only the exact assignment printed by SessionStart. Re-inspect after
each mutation because predecessor tokens deliberately expire instead of last-writer-win.
Navigate explicit provenance with: coherence consequence inspect "work:WORK_ID"

`--over` is repeatable and it is the field that matters most: what you REJECTED is
what stops the next agent re-litigating a settled question. If you rejected nothing,
omit it — an unexamined choice and a forced one should not look alike.

WHEN A NUMBER SURPRISES YOU, DOUBT THE INSTRUMENT BEFORE THE SUBJECT — and record
the question even if you cannot chase it. An unresolved conjecture is a real entry:

  coherence conjecture "<the surprising observation>" --could-be "<explanation>" \
    --discriminated-by "<the test that would separate them>" --session "{{session}}" --agent "{{agent}}"
  coherence resolved <id> --because "<what that test showed>" --as "<which candidate won>" --session "{{session}}" --agent "{{agent}}"
  coherence dismiss <id> --because "<why it is not worth chasing>" --session "{{session}}" --agent "{{agent}}"

You need not supply "the instrument is wrong" — it is added for you. It is the
highest-prior explanation for a surprising measurement and the one everyone skips.

WHEN YOU OBSERVE A DEFECT, RECORD IT BEFORE THE REPAIR ERASES THE EVIDENCE:

  coherence defect "<what failed>" --evidence "<the reproducer, output, or field report>" --session "{{session}}" --agent "{{agent}}"

This is your assessed conclusion, not machine proof. If whether it is a defect is
still an open question, use conjecture instead. Attach each affected path with --file.
Redact credentials, tokens, personal data, and customer data: this record is committed.

`dismiss` is NOT `resolved`. Use it when the question is real and nobody intends to
answer it — it renders in its own section, saying exactly that, and it stops the
advisories re-raising the same finding. Answering something you did not answer is the
one thing this journal cannot recover from.

BEFORE YOU ADD A CONCEPT, COUNT ITS INSTANCES. A mechanism with no subjects in this
project is a FINDING, not a feature — and the finding is usually a subtraction that
does the same work. Record what you measured, what you would have built, and the
QUERY that decided it, because the answer is a function of the project and will change:

  coherence decide "not X — measured N instances" --over "<the mechanism you did not build>" \
    --because "<the query, so the next agent can re-run it instead of re-arguing>" --session "{{session}}" --agent "{{agent}}"

WHEN YOU FIX A BUG, DECIDE WHAT HAPPENS TO ITS CLASS — dissolve > declare > infer.
Best: make the class UNREPRESENTABLE — remove the duplicated state, narrow the type,
collapse the second spelling of the domain that let two copies disagree. Next: PIN it —
an invariant anchored by a boundary whose guard goes red if the class returns, plus a
`## refutations` line recording what you actually observed broken; a fixed bug is a
measured negative control, and it is evidence only if it is written down. A spot fix
is the floor, not the fix — if the stronger rungs were out of reach, say why:

  coherence decide "spot-fixed <bug>; class survives" --over "dissolving <the state that allows it>" \
    --because "<why unrepresentable/pinned was not reachable today>" --session "{{session}}" --agent "{{agent}}"

WHEN YOU FORM A MULTI-STEP PLAN, MAKE ITS PREDICTION FALSIFIABLE before acting:
  coherence experiment create "<what you expect will work>" --context "<file you expect to need>" \
    --action "<planned action>" --success "<observable success criterion>" --session "{{session}}" --agent "{{agent}}"
The command prints stable action/criterion ids and a close template. Closing derives
success, failure, or inconclusive from evidence for EVERY id; a Stop or a checked box
never becomes success by itself.

Two more verbs:
  coherence blocked "<what you could not do>" --because "<why>" --session "{{session}}" --agent "{{agent}}"
  coherence retract <id> --because "<what refuted it>" --session "{{session}}" --agent "{{agent}}"

This gates nothing. It cannot fail your build and it is not a checklist — log the
handful of choices a reader who never saw your transcript would need, not every step.
A job that logs three real decisions is worth more than one that logs thirty steps.

append.text:
COHERENCE MAINTAINER CONTRACT — keep the project hook and packaged hook in step.

If a change adds or changes a public agent-facing command or coordination function,
review whether the global lifecycle instructions must expose it. This includes changes
to command registration, orientation, work, experiments, consequences, and the exact
actions an owner can take from a work order.

Before finishing that change:

- compare the new behavior with `agentInstructions` and `assignedWorkInstructions` in
  `src/hooks.ts`; bounded startup context may omit a capability only by explicit choice;
- when emitted meaning changes, bump `HOOK_BODY_PROTOCOL_VERSION` in `src/control.ts`;
- regenerate both tracked controls with `{{cli}} hooks install --host codex` and
  `{{cli}} hooks install --host claude`;
- update the exact hook/control tests, packed-consumer smoke, README, and generated docs,
  then run both host checks.

Record an intentional omission in the decision journal. Silence must not be the way the
project decides that a new capability does not belong in the global hook.

guarantees.text: Every canonical quantity has one identity, type or unit, admissible domain, and initialization rule.
No presentation, history, persistence, or process component maintains an independently authoritative state copy.
Committed states satisfy finite, range, and declared cross-field constraints.
Snapshots are immutable observations of one coherent logical instant.
Reset restores declared initial state, logical time, stochastic state, and history policy.
The process declares complete inputs and affected canonical quantities.
The process proposes a delta or next-state contribution and cannot privately commit canonical state.
Behavior is defined in terms of an explicit logical timestep.
Equal state, parameters, timestep, and random stream produce equal output.
Transitions cannot introduce invalid, non-finite, or domain-impossible committed state.
Important causal and monotonic directions have explicit falsifiable tests.
Wall clock, DOM, ambient randomness, and mutable globals cannot alter model evolution unnoticed.
Consumers observe pre-step or post-step state, never a partially updated mixture.
Every active process participates exactly once under declared phase and ordering semantics.
Process ordering, simultaneous-delta combination, or convergence semantics are explicit.
Feedback uses a declared old/new-state policy that prevents accidental same-cycle feedback.
Logical model time advances exactly with committed steps.
Repeated executions from the same versioned scenario and seed reproduce the same trajectory.
A failed process cannot leave a partially committed simulation step.
Logical time is independent of rendering; pause advances zero cycles and advance(n) commits exactly n cycles without silent skip or duplication.
Trigger, payload, affected fields, random source, identity, and cycle application point are explicit.
A versioned scenario and seed completely and atomically produce a valid initial world distinct from evolved state.
Parameter units, domains, defaults, versioning, consumers, and cycle-boundary change semantics are explicit and distinct from evolving state.
The observable is a pure deterministic projection with complete declared dependencies and no independent state authority.
Samples identify committed logical instants, cadence, before/after convention, retention, reset/load behavior, and schema compatibility without mutating current state.
The public observation declares exact field paths, names, types, units, nullability, ranges, authority status, snapshot coherence, compatibility policy, and consumer-side negative contract tests.
Observation cannot mutate or influence the simulated trajectory and distinguishes undefined from numeric zero.
Randomness comes only from an explicit owned stream with replayable state and declared consumption semantics.
Timestep and active-process regime changes are explicit and tested at equivalence or declared tolerance boundaries.
Feedback direction, delay, regulation or amplification, and stability expectations have falsifiable cycle tests.
Behavior immediately below, at, and above every named threshold is specified and tested.
Stock and flow residuals close within a declared tolerance with explicit sources and sinks.
Spatial indexing, boundaries, neighborhood semantics, and aggregation consistency are explicit.
Aggregation weights, missing values, units, and consistency with source state are explicit.
External interventions validate authority, timing, cost, affected quantities, and interaction with replay.
Approximation scope, calibration basis, excluded behavior, and invalid inference boundaries are explicit.
Boundary inputs are validated and failures preserve caller-visible semantics.
State transitions have one named authority and reject stale or invalid transitions.
Start, stop, cancellation, failure, and recovery are explicit and idempotent where repeated.
Concurrent operations preserve ordering, ownership, and stale-work exclusion.
Durable authority and rebuildable derived state are distinguished and recovery is testable.
Extension discovery, compatibility, isolation, and failure containment are explicit.
User-visible state has deterministic loading, empty, success, and failure behavior.
Operational signals are bounded, attributable, redactable, and non-authoritative.
The decision is total over its declared input domain, deterministic, side-effect free, and explicit about missing or invalid inputs.
Arguments, exit codes, output channels, interruption, and partial failure form a stable contract.
Logical identity, reconnect, cancellation, and teardown remain distinct from transport ownership.
Construction validates configuration and never leaks a partially initialized product.
